title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 4 findings on PR #524 head fdce24e
description:
Supervisor self-review round 4 of PR #524 head fdce24e. Severity is dropping — round 3 had a HIGH playability regression; this round's worst is MEDIUM, and the sweep independently verified several previously-suspect areas as clean (savepoint-nested position rollback, the recurring-question reclassification agreeing on both sides of the seam, late-join dedup not dropping a placeable ruling, migration/ledger/snapshot consistency).

FOUR findings. Three are consequences of round 3's own fixes. Finding 2 is round 3's finding 2 NOT actually fixed.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev7 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev7, cut from eshyra-jhpt at fdce24e. Run `npm ci` before verification.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (MEDIUM — the real bug this round) — a rule scheduled for a future turn is live or silently dead depending on a value the caller cannot know.
=============================================================
Round 3 finding 5 routed caller-supplied positions through persisted-chronology validation, but assertPersistedPositionAtOrBeforeCurrent deliberately SKIPS validation when the ordinal is above the current one — so a future-dated prospective rule keeps a fabricated sessionId/turnId. compareCampaignPositions tie-breaks equal ordinals on exactly those anchors. So whether the rule is actually in force on the turn that later receives that ordinal depends on a lexicographic comparison against a turn id that did not exist when the rule was written.
REPRODUCED at fdce24e (supervisor), current turn {s, abc, 1}:
    scheduled with fabricated anchor turnId=zzz; real turn 2 turnId=def
    active at real turn 2: []                      <- rule scheduled for this turn is missing
    same rule, fabricated anchor turnId=aaa -> active at real turn 2: [ 'scheduled' ]
Identical rule, opposite outcome, decided by a coin flip. The sweep also found the rule is then un-revocable at that turn: revokeCampaignRule with the REAL ordinal-2 anchor throws 'cannot be revoked before its effective position'.
FIX: a future position has no persisted anchor, so it must not carry a fabricated one that participates in ordering. Either reject future ordinals outright at the mutation boundary, or store a chronology-only anchor for a not-yet-persisted position — an ordinal plus a sentinel session/turn that sorts deterministically ahead of any real anchor for that ordinal — so ordering depends only on the ordinal, which is the authoritative field. State which you chose and why. Whichever you choose, scheduling for a future turn must either work deterministically or be refused; it must not depend on unknowable input.
EVIDENCE: the two cases above must produce the same outcome (both active, or both rejected). Plus revocation at the real anchor must behave consistently.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (round 3 finding 2, NOT fixed) — the probe closure assertion still cannot fail.
=============================================================
Round 3 added m5.ambiguityCoverage, but the underlying problem stands: measurements.ts's early return makes m5.unqueriedAmbiguityIds unconditionally [] in every production trace. runDiscoveryStages calls the first joinCampaignRules without `conditional`, so `asked` is always true and rulingQueryScope is always 'all-active', so the `|| lateRuleJoin` disjunct is never reached. m5.allActiveRulingsRequested is a constant true and ambiguityCoverage a constant 'all-active' — and the NEW probe assertion added in round 3 asserts a constant too. discoveryProbes.test.ts:219's closure invariant ("every ambiguity that reached the packet was offered to the seam") still cannot fail for any input.
This is the same failure mode as round 3's findings 9/10, in the measurement layer: an assertion that is structurally incapable of failing.
FIX: re-express the invariant against what the seam actually RETURNED, not against a scope flag that is short-circuited to a constant. If the invariant is genuinely subsumed by all-active scope, then delete the dead computation and the vacuous assertion and say so explicitly in a comment — do not leave an assertion that looks like a guarantee and is not one. Whatever you choose, demonstrate the probe can fail: temporarily break the property and show the probe catches it, then restore.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 — round 3's collision rejection can brick a campaign, because round 3's degrade only catches binding errors.
=============================================================
Round 3 finding 8 made ambiguitiesFromStack throw CampaignRuleError on a duplicate ambiguity id across record keys. Round 3 finding 1 made contextAssembler degrade — but only for CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError; everything else rethrows. So a pack-authoring mistake (an add-on restating a base ambiguity under a different record key; optRulesAmbiguities enforces id uniqueness only WITHIN a record, and resolveRulesStack merges by record key) hard-fails assemble_context on every turn. That is precisely the bricked-campaign outcome finding 1 was dispatched to eliminate, arriving through the door finding 8 opened.
FIX: a pack-authoring error must degrade, not brick play — the same treatment as an unavailable pack. Surface the collision in the assembled context (both record keys, as the current message already does) and continue, rather than throwing on the per-turn path. Keep a hard error where pack content is validated, not where a turn is assembled.
EVIDENCE: a stack with a colliding ambiguity id assembles successfully, the collision is visible in the context and the rendered prompt, and both record keys are named.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 — N+1 queries on the per-turn hot path, plus two dead indexes.
=============================================================
activeRows already holds every campaign_rule row for the campaign in memory, but for each superseded row it issues a fresh getCampaignRule query from inside the .filter callback to find a successor that is guaranteed to be in that same set (validateCampaignRules enforces same-campaign supersession). assembleCampaignRulesContext calls activeRows twice per turn, so a long-running campaign pays 2 x N_superseded avoidable point queries every turn.
FIX: build a Map<ruleIdentity, row> once from the rows already fetched. Behaviour must not change; this is purely removing redundant queries.
ALSO NOTE (non-blocking, decide and record): migration 0025's campaign_rule_effective_position and campaign_rule_status_position indexes are unused — every read path is WHERE campaign_id = ? with the position predicates evaluated in JS. Do NOT drop them in this PR (that is a migration change on a merged migration); instead say in your notes whether they should be dropped in a follow-up bead, and file it if so.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against fdce24e; report the counts you actually observed. For finding 2, demonstrating the probe CAN fail is the evidence, not a passing run.
  - Every negative assertion you add or touch must assert the distinctive guard message, per the standard established last round.
  - Do not weaken existing tests, do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, or eshyra-umyb.

VERIFICATION
`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local @eshyra/core resolution.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-03: codex gpt-5.6-luna, effort HIGH, YOLO, pgid 1001396, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev7 (cut from eshyra-jhpt @ fdce24e).
Completed in commit 818517d (not pushed; integration owner will pick up the branch).

Fixes: (1) prospective future effective positions are persisted with the reserved __future__ chronology-only anchor, ordered after ordinal comparison and before every real anchor at that ordinal; real-turn revocation now succeeds deterministically. (2) M5 unqueriedAmbiguityIds uses actual seam query arguments plus ambiguity IDs on returned rulings, not the constant all-active scope flag; RuleJoinTrace records returnedAmbiguityIds. (3) duplicate ambiguity IDs raise the narrow CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError and degrade only in per-turn context assembly; the collision text remains visible in assembled context and rendered prompt. (4) activeRows builds row/rule identity maps from the fetched campaign rows and removes superseded-row point queries.
